newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australian minister Prosser resigns - PM.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australian minister Prosser resigns - PM.

text.p: Australia's national minister for small businesses, Geoff Prosser, has resigned from his post, Prime Minister John Howard said on Friday.
Prosser had been under opposition pressure to quit over allegations of conflicts of interest arising from his own business activities.

Howard said that Prosser's duties would be assumed by Industrial Relations Minister Peter Reith, who will retain his current duties and will become Minister for Workplace Relations and Small Business.

"The transfer of the small business responsibility to a senior cabinet minister emphasises the government's strong belief that small business has a critical role to play in the employment and economic future of Australia," Howard said.
As part of a wider reshuffle, Reith's role in helping Howard would be assumed by David Kemp, Minister for Schools Vocational Education and Training.

Western Australian senator Chris Ellison becomes Minister for Customs and Consumer Affairs, a newly-created portfolio. Ellision will also have the additional role of minister assisting the Attorney General.
Neil Andrew, MP for Wakefield, will be the new Chief Government Whip, while Queensland Peter Slipper will become a whip, replacing Trish Worth.
Worth replaces Ellison as parliamentary secretary to the minister for health.
Reith will also retain his duties as leader of the house of representatives, Howard said.
Prosser announced his intention to resign in a letter to Howard released by Howard's office.

"Over the past few weeks, the media and the opposition have sought to make my presence in the Ministry the focus of attention rather than the the broader policy issues and achievements of your Government," Prosser wrote.

"I appreciate that this is now distracting the community and diverting government resources and energy from the central task we have at hand - that of job creation and revitalising the small business sector," he added.
Prosser said he was proud of his achievements in the post but was resigning to "to ensure that the Australian people can have the proper focus on the issues".
He offered his services in any future ministerial post.
Government guidelines bar ministers from daily business activities and from being involved in decisions which could affect their business interests.

The opposition had accused Prosser, who owns shopping malls in Western Australia, of understating the extent of his dealings with Coles Myers Ltd and former senior conservative politician Nick Greiner and of lobbying local government politicians about his businesses.
